Reach a steady, practical space — start the conversation

I work with adults facing anxiety, relationship strain, burnout, and life transitions. If you want clear next steps and steady support, reach out and we'll clarify what a focused path looks like for you.

Prefer to pick a time? Book now →

I typically respond within 48 business hours. If this is an emergency or you are in crisis, please call 911 or your local emergency services. I do not provide crisis services via email or this form.

How I work — values that shape sessions

I bring practical, evidence‑informed approaches with an emphasis on clarity, pacing, and compassionate accountability. Typical values that guide my work:

  • Transparent goals and measurable steps
  • Collaborative planning — you guide priorities
  • Respect for your time and context
  • Careful attention to safety and boundaries

Practical methods I use

I draw from short‑term, skill‑based modalities to keep work focused and actionable. Common methods include:

Cognitive Behavioral Strategies
Trauma‑informed stabilization
Interpersonal practice
Values‑based planning

Modalities: {{MODALITIES}}

Common concerns I hear

It's normal to have questions before starting. Here are a few I often address in early conversations:

  • Will this change feel like therapy forever? Most clients want focused change; I tailor pacing so you can meet short‑term goals and reassess regularly.
  • What if I'm not sure what to say? That's common. Sessions begin with orientation—what matters most to you—then we proceed together.
  • Is this confidential? Yes. Notes are kept in a secure system. Exceptions: imminent risk of harm to self/others, child or elder abuse, or court order.

Client reflections

These brief excerpts reflect the tone of work — thoughtful, pragmatic, steady.

"Working together helped me make a plan I could actually follow. I felt heard and guided." — A client in {{CITY}}
"Practical tools and a calm framework made difficult decisions easier." — Another client

How to move forward

If you'd like to see whether I might be a fit, you can:

  1. Use the form above to send a short note
  2. Book a 15‑minute consultation on the Book page
  3. Call or email if you prefer direct contact

Schedule a 15‑minute consult

Privacy, scope & boundaries

Confidentiality: Communications are treated as clinical records and stored securely. Exceptions to confidentiality include imminent risk of serious harm, suspected abuse of a vulnerable person, or legal obligation.

Scope: I provide outpatient therapy for adults. I do not provide emergency/crisis services, forensic assessments, or court testimony as part of routine therapy. If you require urgent care, please contact local emergency services or a crisis line.
